text:
maria: uploaded a Perfetto trace that shows a weird span merge at the gateway -> runtime handoff. link: https://perfetto.dev/trace/abc123 (private)
maria: short summary: when client chunks cross gateway boundary we sometimes see span A and B merged into one parent during sampling, and that correlates with kernel-selection flipping to quantized path mid-request
kevin: can you paste the perfetto slice names around the merge? are these chunk boundaries or retries?
maria: slices: "client_send", "gateway_slice", "runtime_prefetch", "kernel_select". timestamps show gateway_slice split at 0.003s and runtime_prefetch starts 0.001s before second half arrives. seems like overlapping chunks
akash: looked at nsys recording. Kernel hotpath changes when KV cache miss rate spikes. nvprof shows these kernels: MatMulFused(quant) and MatMulFused(fp16) alternating.
akash: nvprof snippet: 
```
NVIDIA NVPROF: Kernel: MatMulFused_fp16  time=1.2ms
NVIDIA NVPROF: Kernel: MatMulFused_quant time=0.9ms
KVCache Misses: 0 -> 23 -> 1 per request
```

maria: reproduction steps I ran: curl client with two chunked messages (400 + 1200 tokens) -> gateway splits -> runtime gets two incoming RPCs with overlapping lifetimes. Add --enable-prefetch to runtime and you can see the select flip.
kevin: sounds like batching heuristic picks a different kernel when it sees the second incoming chunk in-flight. Could be our kernel selector using instantaneous batch_size instead of reserved/expected size.
akash: yep. in kernel_selection.cc we pick kernel based on current_batch_len and kv_cache_state. If prefetch kicks in early, current_batch_len shows larger effective seq_len and picks quant path which misses in KV index and causes reloads.
maria: attaching quick perfetto screenshot of waterfall and kernel timeline (screenshot id: waterfall-456). Also saw a spike in api.latency tail at 99.9th from 32ms -> 120ms for those traces.
ci-bot: regression detector flagged a 0.8% increase in p99 for client-gateway path for commit c4d2f9b between canary runs.
kevin: plan: add guard to kernel selector to prefer stable batch estimate for first N ms of an rpc or until kv_cache warm. Also try delaying prefetch by 2ms if gateway chunk boundary detected.
maria: I'll open a tiny PR with the guard and a stress job (run nsys on 1000 synthetic chunked requests) and post results.
akash: can you include an nvprof + perfetto pair? nvprof for kernel-level timings and perfetto for spans. I'll diff kernel names across runs.
maria: yep. command I used: `NSYS_PROFILE=1 nsys profile --trace=cuda,osrt --output=run1 ./runtime --enable-prefetch` then `perfetto --serve trace.pb`. attaching run ids.
kevin: also add a unit test that simulates overlapping RPC arrivals and asserts kernel selector stays stable.
maria: noted. setting priority: high. I'll post PR link when ready.
kevin: thanks, this aligns with the batch-selection bug I suspected last week. :thumbsup:
